rv.q: The result is a joyous and sometimes jaw-dropping send-up of high culture.
Warren-Smith is an accomplished, genuinely disarming clown, who knows how to judge his audience and instinctively gets them onside.
What could easily become a chaotic collection of tricks instead develops a fluid, infectious rhythm.
This progressive take on a classic craft is also unexpectedly and weirdly affirming.
This is an hour that you will inevitably spend laughing, and while it may not deepen your understanding of any Penguin Classics, it is arguably more enjoyable than many of them.
This is literature as contact sport, not contemplation, and that’s both its triumph and its trap.
Classic Penguins is the best show yet from Damien Warren-Smith and his hilarious alter-ego Garry Starr, deserving every accolade it receives.
Its gloriously silly and afraid to push the boundaries as far as imaginable.
This blisteringly barmy bonanza is a spectacle of non-stop laughter and joy.
It was hilarious, bizarre, zany, original, surprising, unexpected, and very, very funny.
Warren-Smith commits wholeheartedly to his genre, delivering a madcap show that is more than a performance: it’s an experience — the full package.
In the end Garry Starr: Classic Penguin is more than just a spoof of great literature; it's a celebration of the odd, the bizarre, the utterly human.
Ultimately, humour is highly subjective, and this broad approach may not appeal to everyone.
It's truly a once-in-a-lifetime clown experience, not to be missed if you can help it.
Run, don't waddle, to feeding time at the zoo: two months of this literary lunacy has arrived from Edinburgh to Victoria.

cn.t: Critics hail this gleefully absurd literary romp as brilliantly stupid, with Damien Warren-Smith's full-frontal penguin clown earning raves for its clever wordplay, chaotic physical comedy, and surprising theatrical invention across Penguin Classics.
